title: Psalms Chapter 47 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 47 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 47 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 47.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm for according to Psalms 47:1?
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Korah
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:1 states that this Psalm is for 'the sons of Korah.'

questions.question: What are the people commanded to do to God in Psalms 47:1?
options: Clap hands and shout with the voice of triumph
questions.correctAnswer: Clap hands and shout with the voice of triumph
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:1 commands all people to 'O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:2, how is the LORD described?
questions.correctAnswer: Most high and terrible
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:2 says 'For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth.'

questions.question: What title is given to God in Psalms 47:2?
options: Great King over all the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Great King over all the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:2 describes God as 'a great King over all the earth.'

questions.question: What does God do with the people according to Psalms 47:3?
options: He shall subdue the people under us
He shall scatter the people abroad
He shall teach the people His laws
questions.correctAnswer: He shall subdue the people under us
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:3 states 'He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:1 calls on all people to shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:1 explicitly says 'O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:3 says God will bless the nations without subduing them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:3 says that God 'shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet,' not just bless them.

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:4, what has God chosen for us?
questions.correctAnswer: Our inheritance
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 reads 'He shall choose our inheritance for us, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved.'

questions.question: What is the 'excellency' mentioned in Psalms 47:4 referring to?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob whom God loved
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 specifies that the inheritance is 'the excellency of Jacob whom he loved.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:5 describes God as going up with the sound of a trumpet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:5 states, 'God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.'

questions.question: In Psalms 47:6, how many times are we instructed to sing praises to God?
questions.correctAnswer: Four times
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:6 says, 'Sing praises to God, sing praises: sing praises unto our King, sing praises.' The phrase 'sing praises' is repeated four times.

questions.question: Which of these instructions appears first in Psalms 47?
options: Clap your hands, all ye people
God is gone up with a shout
questions.correctAnswer: Clap your hands, all ye people
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:1 begins with 'O clap your hands, all ye people;' which comes before the other instructions found in later verses.

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:7, what should accompany singing praises to God?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:7 instructs, 'sing ye praises with understanding.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:8 says God sitteth upon the throne of his mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:8 says God 'sitteth upon the throne of his holiness,' not mercy.

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:9, what belongs to God?
questions.correctAnswer: The shields of the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:9 states, 'for the shields of the earth belong unto God.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 47 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 47 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:4, what has God chosen for His people?
options: Their inheritance, the excellency of Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: Their inheritance, the excellency of Jacob
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 states that God shall choose our inheritance, specifically mentioning the excellency of Jacob whom He loved, showing God’s promise to His chosen people.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:5 describe God's ascension?
options: God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet
God rose like the morning sun
God appeared in a pillar of fire
questions.correctAnswer: God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:5 vividly describes God’s ascension using the imagery of a shout and trumpet sound, symbolizing triumph and divine authority.

questions.question: What repeated action does Psalms 47:6 encourage believers to perform?
questions.correctAnswer: Sing praises to God
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:6 twice commands to 'sing praises' to God and the King, emphasizing joyful worship as a vital Christian practice.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is emphasized by the call to 'sing praises with understanding' in Psalms 47:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom and heartfelt worship
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:7 calls for praising God 'with understanding,' highlighting the importance of worshiping God wisely and sincerely, connecting knowledge with devotion.

questions.question: What does Psalms 47:8 say about God's reign?
options: God reigneth over the heathen and sitteth upon the throne of his holiness
questions.correctAnswer: God reigneth over the heathen and sitteth upon the throne of his holiness
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereign rule over all nations (heathen) and His holy throne, teaching believers about God's universal authority and purity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 47:9 teach about the role of earthly rulers in relation to God?
options: They are gathered as the people of the God of Abraham, and the shields of the earth belong to God
They rule by their own wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: They are gathered as the people of the God of Abraham, and the shields of the earth belong to God
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:9 shows that earthly princes and peoples are united under God’s protection and authority, reinforcing the truth that all power ultimately belongs to God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 47:5 say will happen when God ascends with a shout and trumpet sound, and how does this connect to Psalms 47:6?
options: God's triumphant ascension inspires believers to sing praises to Him
God’s ascension causes fear and trembling, so believers must be silent
God's ascension is a secret event unrelated to worship
God ascends to punish, so believers should repent
questions.correctAnswer: God's triumphant ascension inspires believers to sing praises to Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:5 describes God's triumphant ascension with a shout and trumpet, which naturally leads to the call in Psalms 47:6 for believers to sing praises, showing worship as a response to God's majesty.

questions.question: If believers follow Psalms 47:1 by clapping hands and shouting to God, what does Psalms 47:2 say about the nature of the LORD they are praising?
options: The LORD most high is terrible and a great King over all the earth
The LORD is distant and unapproachable
The LORD is a quiet shepherd
The LORD is only a local deity
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD most high is terrible and a great King over all the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:2 explains that the LORD praised in verse 1 is the Most High, fearsome in power, and sovereign over all the earth, encouraging reverent worship.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles to trust God’s sovereignty over nations. Based on Psalms 47:3 and 47:4, what truth can encourage them?
options: God subdues the nations and chooses our inheritance, showing His control and love
God is distant from earthly affairs
Nations are ruled by chance, not God
We must rely on human strength to overcome nations
questions.correctAnswer: God subdues the nations and chooses our inheritance, showing His control and love
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:3 shows God's power to subdue peoples and nations, while 47:4 affirms His loving choice of our inheritance, offering assurance of His sovereign care.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:6 teach the importance of worshiping God in our daily lives?
options: By instructing to 'sing praises' repeatedly, it encourages continual joyful worship
It suggests worship only on special occasions
It emphasizes silent meditation instead of singing
It teaches that worship is optional
questions.correctAnswer: By instructing to 'sing praises' repeatedly, it encourages continual joyful worship
questions.explanation: The repetition in Psalms 47:6 highlights singing praises as a continual, joyful act, teaching believers to maintain a heart of worship daily.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:7 teaches that praise should be given with understanding, meaning worship without knowledge is insufficient.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:7 explicitly commands singing praises 'with understanding,' implying that meaningful knowledge and awareness are essential in worship.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:9 says that the shields of the earth belong to the kings and princes, not to God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:9 states that 'the shields of the earth belong unto God,' meaning all protection and power belong to God, not to earthly rulers.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:8 declares that God sits upon the throne of his holiness and reigns over the heathen, showing His universal sovereignty.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:8 clearly emphasizes God's universal reign and holy authority, asserting His sovereignty over all nations.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trust in God’s choices can be drawn from Psalms 47:4?
options: Trust that God chooses the best inheritance for His people, reflecting His love
Trust human wisdom over divine guidance
Trust that inheritance is earned by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: Trust that God chooses the best inheritance for His people, reflecting His love
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 teaches believers to trust in God’s loving choice of their inheritance, assuring them of His good and perfect will.

questions.question: How does the imagery in Psalms 47:5 of God ascending 'with a shout' and 'the sound of a trumpet' relate to Christian hope?
options: It symbolizes victorious triumph and the promised return of Christ
It describes a past event unrelated to future hope
It is a metaphor for quiet meditation
It teaches that God is silent in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes victorious triumph and the promised return of Christ
questions.explanation: The shout and trumpet in Psalms 47:5 symbolize victory and divine authority, pointing forward to the hope of Christ’s triumphant return.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 47 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 47.

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:7, what characteristic should accompany singing praises to God?
questions.correctAnswer: With understanding
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:7 states explicitly, "sing ye praises with understanding," indicating that worship should be thoughtful and aware.

questions.question: What is described as God’s seat in Psalms 47:8?
questions.correctAnswer: The throne of his holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:8 says, "God sitteth upon the throne of his holiness," emphasizing God's pure and sovereign rule.

questions.question: Who are gathered together in Psalms 47:9?
questions.correctAnswer: The princes of the people
questions.explanation: The verse states, "The princes of the people are gathered together, even the people of the God of Abraham," highlighting a unification of leaders under God’s sovereignty.

questions.question: Which phrase from Psalms 47:9 signifies God’s protection over the earth?
options: The shields of the earth belong unto God
The mountains bow down before Him
The sun and moon obey His command
questions.correctAnswer: The shields of the earth belong unto God
questions.explanation: This phrase from Psalms 47:9 conveys that God is the protector and defender, a common theme also echoed in Exodus 15:3 where God is called "a man of war."

questions.question: Psalms 47:7 declares God as King of all the earth. Which New Testament verse echoes this universal kingship?
questions.correctAnswer: Philippians 2:10-11
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:10-11 declares that every knee should bow to Jesus, affirming God’s universal kingship as in Psalms 47:7.

questions.question: The term 'heathen' in Psalms 47:8 refers to:
questions.correctAnswer: Nations outside Israel
questions.explanation: In Psalms 47:8, 'heathen' (Hebrew 'goyim') typically refers to Gentile nations, illustrating God's reign over all peoples, not just Israel.

questions.question: The phrase 'God is gone up with a shout' in Psalms 47:5 likely symbolizes:
options: The blowing of the ram’s horn
questions.correctAnswer: God’s ascension or exaltation
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:5 uses this phrase to describe God's triumphant exaltation, which parallels the ascension of Christ in Acts 1:9.

questions.question: The repetition of 'sing praises' in Psalms 47:6 is an example of which Hebrew literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase "sing praises" in Psalms 47:6 exemplifies Hebrew parallelism, emphasizing the call to worship fully and joyfully.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47 was written by the sons of Korah according to the heading in verse 1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The heading in Psalms 47:1 states, "A Psalm for the sons of Korah," indicating the traditional authorship or association.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 47:4 claims that God chose the inheritance of Esau for His people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 specifically says God chose "the excellency of Jacob whom he loved," not Esau, signifying God's covenant with Israel.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:8 portray God’s reign in relation to holiness?
options: God sits upon the throne of his holiness
God’s holiness is hidden from the nations
God’s throne is in the temple alone
Holiness is separate from God’s reign
questions.correctAnswer: God sits upon the throne of his holiness
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes God's pure and sacred rule by stating He "sitteth upon the throne of his holiness," showing that holiness is intrinsic to His kingship.

questions.question: What theme in Psalms 47 is fulfilled in Revelation 19:6 about God's reign?
options: God is King of all the earth
God creates a new heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: God is King of all the earth
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:6 echoes the universal kingship theme of Psalms 47:7 by proclaiming "the Lord God omnipotent reigneth."

questions.question: The phrase 'the shields of the earth' in Psalms 47:9 primarily symbolizes:
options: Physical weapons used in ancient warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection over nations
questions.explanation: In Psalms 47:9, 'shields of the earth' metaphorically represents God's defense and sovereignty over the peoples of the earth.

questions.question: The shout and trumpet sound in Psalms 47:5 likely allude to which Old Testament event?
options: The giving of the Law at Mount Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: The fall of Jericho’s walls
questions.explanation: The shout and trumpet in Psalms 47:5 recall the battle at Jericho (Joshua 6), where trumpets and shouting signified divine victory and presence.

questions.question: Which New Testament concept is foreshadowed by God’s universal kingship in Psalms 47:7-8?
options: The reign of Christ as King of kings
The parables of Jesus about the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The reign of Christ as King of kings
questions.explanation: The universal reign of God in Psalms 47 anticipates the New Testament depiction of Christ reigning over all (1 Timothy 6:15).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 47 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 47 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted by the phrase 'For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth'?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:2 emphasizes God's supreme rule and authority over all the earth, revealing His sovereignty as the great King over all nations.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the statement 'He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet'?
options: The universal reign of Christ over all peoples
The final judgment on the wicked
The promise of Israel's earthly conquest
The establishment of the church as a political kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The universal reign of Christ over all peoples
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:3 reveals the doctrine of Christ's universal reign where all nations are subdued under His authority, affirming His lordship over all humanity (cf. Philippians 2:9-11).

questions.question: According to Psalms 47:4, what is the significance of 'the excellency of Jacob whom he loved'?
options: It refers to the exclusive salvation of Israel
It highlights God's covenantal election of Israel
It denotes Israel's political supremacy over other nations
It indicates a future messianic kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights God's covenantal election of Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:4 teaches the doctrine of divine election as God chooses Israel ('Jacob') as His inheritance, showing His covenant love and faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained from the depiction of God 'gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet'?
options: God’s enthronement and victory over evil
The call to repentance through prophetic warning
questions.correctAnswer: God’s enthronement and victory over evil
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:5 symbolically portrays God's exaltation and triumph, often associated with divine kingship and victory over enemies, foreshadowing Christ's ascension and reign (cf. Ephesians 4:8).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about worship do Psalms 47:6 and Psalms 47:7 convey?
options: Worship must be joyful and informed
Only the Levites are authorized to worship
Worship is a private, silent act
questions.correctAnswer: Worship must be joyful and informed
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 command singing praises to God 'with understanding,' teaching that worship is both heartfelt (joyful) and intellectual (informed), reflecting true reverence.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:8 reveal God's holiness in relation to His kingship?
options: God’s kingship is separate from His moral perfection
God’s reign is established on His throne of holiness
God’s holiness causes Him to reject kingship
questions.correctAnswer: God’s reign is established on His throne of holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:8 states that God 'sitteth upon the throne of his holiness,' teaching that His sovereign rule is inseparable from His perfect holiness and moral purity.

questions.question: What does the gathering of 'the princes of the people... the people of the God of Abraham' signify in Psalms 47:9?
options: The unity of the covenant community under God’s protection
The political alliance of earthly kingdoms
The division between Israel and other nations
The fall of the nations opposing God
questions.correctAnswer: The unity of the covenant community under God’s protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:9 depicts the gathering of God's covenant people, indicating their unity and divine protection as 'the shields of the earth belong unto God,' affirming God’s providential care.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is emphasized by the phrase 'God is the King of all the earth' in Psalms 47:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:7 declares God's universal kingship, underscoring His omnipotence as the sovereign ruler over the entire earth, exercising supreme power.

questions.question: What synthesis about God's kingship and people’s worship emerges from Psalms 47:1 and Psalms 47:9?
options: God’s kingship calls for joyous communal worship and gathering of His people
God’s kingship is unrelated to human worship
Worship is only for individuals, not groups
God’s people are scattered and do not gather
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingship calls for joyous communal worship and gathering of His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:1 calls all people to clap hands and shout to God, while verse 9 describes the gathering of princes and people, teaching that God’s kingship invites joyful corporate worship and unity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:4 and Psalms 47:8 together illustrate the relationship between divine election and holiness?
options: God chooses His people based on their holiness
God’s chosen inheritance is linked to His holy throne and character
Divine election is unrelated to God’s holiness
Holiness is a human achievement apart from election
questions.correctAnswer: God’s chosen inheritance is linked to His holy throne and character
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows God choosing 'the excellency of Jacob,' while verse 8 emphasizes God sitting on the 'throne of his holiness,' teaching that election is rooted in God’s holy nature and sovereign will.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 47:3’s depiction of subduing nations is merely political boasting without spiritual significance. What does Psalms 47:3 actually teach about God's reign?
options: It reveals God's spiritual dominion and fulfillment of Messianic rule
It is purely historical and lacks theological meaning
It predicts the end of all kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God's spiritual dominion and fulfillment of Messianic rule
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:3 speaks of God's subduing nations under His people, which is a prophetic declaration of God's sovereign spiritual reign through the Messiah, not mere political boasting (cf. Daniel 7:14).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about divine protection is given by the phrase 'the shields of the earth belong unto God' in Psalms 47:9?
options: God alone provides true protection to His people
Human armies are the ultimate shield
We must rely on political alliances for safety
questions.correctAnswer: God alone provides true protection to His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 47:9 declares that 'the shields of the earth belong unto God,' teaching the doctrine that God is the ultimate protector and defender of His covenant people, beyond human means.

questions.question: How does Psalms 47:5 and Psalms 47:6 together inform the Christian understanding of worship's form and purpose?
options: Worship is both expressive (shout and trumpet) and vocal (singing praises)
Worship should be silent and contemplative
Worship is only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Worship is both expressive (shout and trumpet) and vocal (singing praises)
questions.explanation: Verse 5 depicts God’s ascension with a shout and trumpet sound, while verse 6 commands singing praises, teaching that worship involves joyful, expressive, and vocal celebration of God’s kingship.

questions.question: What narrative theological role does Psalms 47 play in the grand biblical story of redemption?
options: It affirms God’s sovereign kingship and the establishment of His kingdom through His chosen people
It focuses solely on individual morality
It predicts the destruction of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God’s sovereign kingship and the establishment of His kingdom through His chosen people
questions.explanation: Throughout Psalms 47, God’s sovereign reign and election of Israel are emphasized, which fits the biblical redemptive narrative of God establishing His kingdom through His covenant people and ultimately through Christ.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine kingship and worship with understanding is drawn from Psalms 47:7 and Psalms 47:1?
options: God’s kingship demands intelligent and joyful praise from all peoples
Only the priests may worship God
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingship demands intelligent and joyful praise from all peoples
questions.explanation: Verse 1 calls all people to clap and shout, while verse 7 commands singing praises with understanding, teaching that worship before the universal King must be both joyful and thoughtful.
